_note: Shown by the menu's Resources and sources button (scripts/ui/sources.gd). Keep it honest: say what is real, what is rounded, and what is invented for gameplay. Every url was checked (HTTP 200) on 14 Nov 2026, including the ones added later that day; check again before the final submission. The missions' own sources are in each level file's based_on block and are listed automatically.
accuracy: Real physics: one low Earth orbit at about 550 km takes about 95 minutes, and the Earth hides the Sun for up to about 35 of them. That is why every satellite needs a battery.
Real rules: CubeSats come in standard sizes (1U is a 10 cm cube, 3U is three of them), and a rideshare rocket sells a slot with a hard mass limit.
Real process: build, test, licence and ship really do run in that order, and radio and imaging licences can take months.
Real launch stages: max-Q, the second-stage burn and separation are the moments a real launch is most likely to go wrong.
Rounded: part masses, power and data rates are in the right range for CubeSat parts, but rounded so the maths is easy.
Invented for gameplay: prices, the exact risk rules, fuel use and the event cards. They teach the trade-off, not the exact number.
Checked: CubeSat sizes and mass limits come from the CubeSat Design Specification Rev 14.1 (the game uses the older, tighter limits on purpose).

The NASA problem: the setting is sourced (south pole lighting, VIPER, IPEx). Only the structured-light 97% is a measured detection rate, so the other sensors are shown as Covered / Weak / Blind, not as percentages.
Every screen with made-up numbers says PLACEHOLDER or ILLUSTRATIVE NUMBERS.
